questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain. Low beams help you see the road without reflecting off the wet surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Detour.
questions.explanation: This orange sign tells drivers to take a different route. Construction zones are dangerous. Orange signs warn you about construction work and direct you away from the main road.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights stop working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light does not work, treat it like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system in your vehicle is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak lets these gases enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is poisonous. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Drivers must obey them. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: You are turning onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
Traffic flows in only one direction on this road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you may cross it to pass slower vehicles when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not turn right on red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn right on red.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. It is posted at traffic lights where you are not allowed to turn right when the light is red.

questions.question: You come to a complete stop at an intersection. You yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then you go when it is safe. Which traffic light means this?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean? Unless a police officer tells you to stop, you may only stop:

options.text: To avoid a crash with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a crash with another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Why should drivers watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers say they were looking but did not see them. These road users are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may move faster and have less noticeable lights. Drivers must always watch carefully for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When you are entering a street from a garage or alley.
When another driver is on your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrive at the same time.
When your traffic light is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians who are on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look like drunk drivers.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look like drunk drivers.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look like drunk drivers. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to keep a drowsy driver safe and alert.

questions.question: When a bus signals to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let the driver know you are there.
Speed up to pass the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the bus.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to merge back onto the main road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely return to traffic.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic that moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip the road better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other dangerous conditions. Winter driving is hard and needs extra care. Check your antifreeze and washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane which direction they must go. Drivers must follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination quickly.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Stay farther away from the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop if needed.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you see rain, snow, or ice on the road, slow down immediately. Slippery conditions may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter a full parking lot.
Do not enter a road construction area.
Do not enter a dead-end street.
Do not enter from this direction on one-way streets or expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter from this direction on one-way streets or expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic on this road moves in one direction only. You cannot enter from where you are. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before you change lanes on a residential street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can be hidden in your blind spot. Always look over your shoulder before you change lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes or turning on a residential street. Signal 5 seconds in advance when changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Side of the road with the lightest traffic.
Same side of the road where traffic is moving.
Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
Side of the road with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they can see oncoming traffic in the nearest lane.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers should go slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that forbid actions are rectangular with white backgrounds and red and black markings. A red circle with a slash over a black symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane will end soon. Drivers in the right lane must move left to stay on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on this road. When it rains, snows, or roads are icy, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not drive in these areas. Trucks are bigger and heavier, so they need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.
